name: Adam Wagner

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and a junior agent at the contact centre, doing calls and chats about orders. I finished secondary school and earn about the usual rate here. I still need help on tangled accounts and my call time is longer than the team target. I use AI every day to draft notes and find policy pages, then check the answer myself.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Celia, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. She works at a clinic desk, and we have about three months of expenses saved. There are some other centres close enough to try. I like testing a new tool on a spare call, but getting the children to school before my shift is the part of the day that runs like a machine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau sounds like our current draft and search tools: small help if someone checks the order. I would show newer agents how to compare a draft with the real delivery page.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job stays, but the mortgage and school costs still matter. Three months saved helps with one surprise, not a long spell without Celia’s clinic wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls, using AI drafts and checking every delivery date. In the first year of small change, I’d put the money from two bought lunches a week into our mortgage reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the household, calm about the work itself. An extra minute checking a customer’s address can save a second call to the contact centre.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What error showed you the need to check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I once almost sent a replacement parcel to the old street because the draft copied an earlier address. I opened the current order and caught it before the customer waited another week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the savings target change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Celia (my partner) and I would keep our three-month reserve in a separate account. I would add the lunch money after payday, not count it until it is there.

I’d show newer agents the **delivery page** before trusting a draft.
think: I think my **job remains** under a small change.
I still watch **mortgage and school costs** with only three months saved.
do: Keep **taking calls** and checking AI dates in 2026.
Move **bought-lunch money** into the mortgage reserve during the first year.
feel: **Uneasy** about household money, calm about work.
S0.quote: An extra minute checking a customer’s address can save a second call to the contact centre.
fieldNote: His **source checks** follow a nearly misdirected parcel.
The **three-month reserve** eases but does not remove household worries.
He chooses a small **lunch saving** rather than changing the family budget broadly.

steps.text: Keep taking calls and checking AI delivery dates against orders
Save the cost of two weekly bought lunches toward the mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will move standard answers first, and junior agents should get paid time on hard cases before those chats vanish. I would ask for a trial with real errors, not only a speed chart.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my routine chats may go before I am quick at disputes. Celia’s clinic pay is steady, but it cannot cover our mortgage and school costs alone; another centre may be using the same software.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d take a paid trial of the new answer tool if offered, logging wrong delivery dates beside a skilled agent. In the first year routine chats move, I’d apply for a posted service-desk role with written hours that cover the mortgage and take paid difficult-case practice if the centre provides it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, because my weak spot becomes the whole shift. I can learn a tool fast, but the wage depends on an employer giving me time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the tool trial measure?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would test ten delivery answers and write down whether the tool chose the current address. If the trial is unpaid, I would keep my normal paid calls instead.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you learn the harder calls?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for one paid dispute shift a month beside a strong agent. A course without a posted job would take time away from the children and still leave my wage unclear.

say: I’d ask for **paid hard-case time** before easy chats disappear.
I’d request **real-error trials** rather than speed charts.
think: I think my **routine chats** may vanish before I master disputes.
I know Celia’s **clinic pay** cannot carry our mortgage alone.
do: Test **ten delivery answers** on paid time if offered in 2026.
Seek **posted desk work** and paid dispute practice during the first year.
feel: **Anxious** about losing the easy part of the job.
S1.quote: I can learn a tool fast, but the wage depends on an employer giving me time.
fieldNote: He tests a **new tool** against current delivery addresses.
His **junior skill gap** matters when simple chats leave.
He requires **paid practice** before counting on harder dispute work.

steps.text: Test ten delivery answers with the new tool on paid time if offered
Take monthly paid dispute practice beside a skilled agent if provided
Apply for a posted service-desk role with mortgage-covering written hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could handle our calls and the checking too. I would ask management for posted human jobs and notice dates before the queue moves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could take almost my full shift in 2028. Robots around 2031 do not buy time for a headset job; our three-month reserve would shrink quickly under the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d stop planning a new garden fence, save any extra shift pay and ask for the staffing plan in writing. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid front-desk job only if its hours cover the mortgage, and use savings while interviewing rather than leave without an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, but I can count what we have and start applying. Three months of mortgage money is a search window, not a new career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say about the fence?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Celia (my partner) the fence can wait another season. The children can still play outside, and the money can stay where the mortgage payment comes from.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would front-desk work really solve it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take a paid front-desk post if the written hours and wage cover our house costs. I would not call another screen job permanent protection from full AGI.

say: I’d request **posted human jobs** and notice dates.
I’d say the **2028 thinking-work date** reaches our calls first.
think: I think AGI could take **almost my full shift**.
I see **three months saved** as search time, not a replacement wage.
do: Delay the **fence** and save extra shift pay for the mortgage in 2026.
Apply for **posted front-desk work** after 2028 only with written mortgage-covering hours and wages.
Keep my **current wage** while interviewing; leave only after a real offer.
S2.quote: Three months of mortgage money is a search window, not a new career.
fieldNote: He understands the **2028 software date** governs his headset work.
He knows a **front-desk role** is a bridge, not guaranteed safety.

steps.text: Delay building a garden fence to keep mortgage cash
Put extra shift pay into the mortgage reserve from 2026
Apply for posted front-desk work with written mortgage-covering hours and wages; leave only after an offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives time to test whether the centre will pay people for the difficult work it keeps. I would ask for a vacancy with wages before taking a course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn account disputes in five years, but I do not know if a desk that checks software will remain staffed after full AGI. Three months saved is not enough to fund a long unpaid change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take one paid difficult-case shift monthly if offered and keep a record of the disputes I resolved. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for a posted paid account-review job whose written wage and hours cover the mortgage, and take a short course only if the hiring employer funds it for that opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years lets me build evidence on real cases. I would rather show an employer a fixed account than a course badge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your case record show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would record the wrong amount, the corrected amount and whether the customer called again. A hiring manager can see whether I actually found a problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for a course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Celia (my partner) and I would keep the reserve for the mortgage. If a course needed fees from us without a hiring employer, we would pass it by.

say: I’d ask for **paid difficult-case work** while agents still have a wage to learn on.
I’d ask for **vacancies and wages** before a course.
think: I think I could learn **account disputes** by 2031.
I doubt a review desk offers **permanent safety** after AGI.
do: Take monthly paid **difficult-case shifts** if offered from 2026.
Apply for **posted review work** after 2031 only with written wages and hours covering the mortgage.
Take a **short course** only if the hiring employer funds it for that opening.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to build case evidence.
S3.quote: I would rather show an employer a fixed account than a course badge.
fieldNote: His **case record** tracks corrected amounts and repeat calls.

steps.text: Take one monthly paid difficult-case shift if the centre offers it

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives agents a decade to learn and employers a decade to show which jobs really pay. I would still ask for paid time on hard accounts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could get good at disputes by 53 and save more. Full thinking AI may still take calls in 2036, while robots come around 2039; I would plan for the earlier change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls, put a fixed amount from each pay into savings and take paid dispute practice if offered. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for a posted service role only if my call hours fall and the written pay covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far end, but the mortgage still makes me watch next month’s roster. A decade before AGI in 2036 does not give my family a decade without bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you practise monthly?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep a small notebook of disputed accounts and practise one new exception each month on a paid shift. I do better when I can see the rule against a real case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not move the children’s school for a vague opening. Celia (my partner) and I would need a signed offer and a school route that works before moving.

I’d say employers must show **real wages** before old jobs change.
think: I think I could master **disputes** and save more by 53.
I still see **2036 thinking AI** as a threat to calls.
do: Keep **taking calls**, save each pay and practise on paid time if offered.
Seek **posted service work** after 2036 if hours fall and pay covers the mortgage.
S4.quote: A decade before AGI in 2036 does not give my family a decade without bills.
fieldNote: He uses **monthly case practice** to build skill gradually.

steps.text: Keep taking calls while the centre staffs them

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because nearly all my calls and chats are thinking work, and my skill with today’s tools does not secure tomorrow’s wage. I would need posted work with mortgage-covering hours, paid time to learn it, and notice before the roster falls.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: I wish you had asked whether speed is the right test. I have fixed a wrong address by taking an extra minute, and that minute saved a second call.

headlineQuote: I have fixed a wrong address by taking an extra minute, and that minute saved a second call.
portrait: At **43**, Adam is a junior call agent after secondary school, still slow on tangled accounts.
He and Celia support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with three months of expenses saved.
He uses **AI daily** and tests tools early while checking the source record.
He needs **paid learning** and posted work with mortgage-covering hours if calls shrink.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could take his screen work before a new role preserves household income.
whatWouldHelp: **Notice**, paid practice and posted work with mortgage-covering hours would help.
